title: The Potions Lab
strapline: Fizz, foam and mysterious brews — bicarb, vinegar and a child completely in charge of the reaction.
intent: Mixing potions puts children in charge of dramatic, cause-and-effect reactions — a spoon of this, a splash of that, and it fizzes — which is thrilling, memorable science.
Measuring, pouring and combining ingredients builds fine-motor control and early ideas of quantity, more and less.
Predicting and testing what will make the biggest fizz, or the brightest brew, is real scientific enquiry with instant, exciting feedback.
The lab is rich in language — bubble, fizz, foam, overflow, react, ingredient — all anchored in something happening in front of them.
Inventing and naming their own potions and recipes fuels imagination, agency and pride in a creation that is entirely theirs.
It is open-ended and no-fail — every brew does something — so all children can succeed and lead their own experiments.
implementation: Set up a lab with bicarbonate of soda, vinegar, washing-up liquid, coloured water, droppers, spoons, pots and trays.
Show the classic fizz once, then hand it over: 'what do you want to try, and what do you think will happen?'
Encourage prediction and comparison: 'which made a bigger fizz — more vinegar or more powder?'
Give real vocabulary as it happens — react, bubble, overflow — and let children start to use it.
Invite children to invent, name and 'record' their potions on a clipboard, drawing what went in.
Keep it safe and taste-free, and let the children run the experiments while you wonder alongside.
key_questions: What do you want to try, and what do you think will happen?
Which made a bigger fizz — more vinegar or more powder?
What shall we call your potion?
What happens if we add just a little, then a lot?
Why do you think it overflowed?

impact.text: Children cause dramatic, cause-and-effect reactions — thrilling, memorable science.
Children measure, pour and combine, building fine-motor control and early ideas of quantity.
Children predict and test what makes the biggest fizz — real scientific enquiry with instant feedback.
Children invent, name and 'record' their own potions, fuelling imagination, agency and pride.
Children gain vocabulary anchored in what's happening — bubble, fizz, foam, overflow, react.

enhancements: Bicarbonate of soda, vinegar, washing-up liquid, coloured water, droppers and trays.
A clipboard for children to draw and 'record' what went into each potion.
A prediction-and-compare challenge — which mix makes the biggest fizz.
Coloured water and glitter to make the brews brighter.
A recipe wall where children name and display their inventions.

playing_exploring: Children combine ingredients freely, thrilled by the fizz and foam each brew produces.
The lab is open-ended and irresistible — every mixture does something worth watching.
active_learning: Children pursue a goal — the biggest fizz, a particular colour — and keep refining the mix to reach it.
creating_thinking: Children predict, test and compare reactions, working out what to add more of to change the result.
